summary: Collapse Settings > About > Diagnostics behind a disclosure that previews its own contents, remembers the user's choice, and forces itself open on a translated build so the one actionable diagnostic is never hidden.

reactNativeIos.reason: The React Native client has no About or diagnostics surface. `getDiagnostics` is an Electron-only IPC handler reading Electron process metrics and GPU feature status, and apps/mobile never calls it: there is no occurrence of getDiagnostics or a diagnostics screen anywhere under apps/mobile/src.

nativeAndroid.reason: The native Android client has no About or diagnostics surface. Its ui package contains no settings-about screen that renders host process metrics, and nothing in apps/android calls the diagnostics contract.

storageDataMigration.reason: No schema change and no migration. The open/closed preference is one row in the existing key-value `settings` table under `about.diagnosticsExpanded`. An absent key already means 'no preference' and resolves to collapsed, so an older database and an older client both behave correctly with no backfill, and a newer database is readable by an older client that simply ignores the key.

updateRelease.reason: Renderer presentation change only. No package identity, signing, deep-link scheme, update channel, IPC channel, or wire-protocol change; the diagnostics IPC contract and its payload are untouched.

automated: npm run typecheck passed for both the main and renderer projects.
npm test passed 378 files / 3,611 tests with 3 skipped on this branch, including 15 new disclosure-policy tests and 10 new first-frame render tests.
tests/unit/diagnostics-disclosure.test.ts pins the gist text, the singular/plural and unknown-count terminal cases, and the rule that a translated build overrides a stored 'false' preference.

tests/unit/diagnostics-section-render.test.ts renders the real component with renderToStaticMarkup and asserts the first frame is collapsed: aria-expanded=false, grid-template-rows:0fr, the body inert, and no process rows painted.
notExercised: The collapse and expand animation, the chevron rotation, and the hover state have not been watched by a human in the running app.
The translated/Rosetta force-open path has not been exercised on an x64 build running under Apple silicon translation; it is covered by unit tests only, because this host runs the native arm64 build.
Persistence across an app restart has not been exercised manually; the settings read and write are covered only by the unit-level key assertion.
Behaviour under prefers-reduced-motion has not been verified visually.

tests/unit/tcp-host.test.ts timed out once at its 5s limit during a full-suite run and passed in isolation and on the clean re-run; it is a real-socket test and load-sensitive, and it is unrelated to this change.
